basic_identification.full_title: Specification for PVC Insulated (Heavy Duty) Electric Cables (विद्युत केबलों के लिए पीवीसी इंसुलेटेड (भारी काम) विशिष्टि)
basic_identification.sector_category: Electrotechnical / Power Cables (approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council and finalized by the Power Cables Sectional Committee, ETD 09, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard series prescribes the manufacturing requirements, material specifications, design configurations, dimensions, safety requirements, and performance testing protocols for PVC-insulated (heavy-duty) electric power and control cables used in fixed installations. Part 1 covers cables with rated voltages up to and including 1100 V (Uo/U = 650/1100 V), and Part 2 covers cables with working voltages from 3.3 kV up to and including 11 kV.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Material and Quality Specification (Electrotechnical Department / Power Cables)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Mandatory Certification under the national Cables (Quality Control) Order. Stamping or embossing of the physical ISI Standard Mark logo on the outer sheath is a statutory requirement to legally manufacture, sell, or distribute heavy-duty cables in India.

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, conductor resistance, insulation thickness, test voltages, and temperatures must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
Conductors must consist of high-purity, plain or tinned annealed copper (solid/stranded) or aluminum wire as per IS 8130, ensuring low electrical resistance and high current-carrying capacity.
Cables are insulated with PVC compound Type A (for normal operation up to 70°C) or Type C (for heat-resistant operations up to 85°C) conforming to IS 5831.

Under active Amendments (Amendment 5 for Part 1, Amendment 4 for Part 2), the armour wires or formed flat strips must be applied closely with a minimum coverage of 90 percent, calculated as per the spiral projection formulas in Appendix C.

Armour percentage is calculated as: Percent coverage = (N * d / W) * 100, where N is wire count, d is wire diameter/width, W = π * D * cos(a), D is diameter under armour, and a is laying pitch angle (tan a = π * D / C, where C is lay length).

Under active Amendments, successful type testing of a cable with a specific conductor cross-sectional area and rated voltage grants valid type approval for other sizes and/or voltages of the same design family, provided insulation material/process match and the area is not larger than the tested cable.
For low-voltage heavy duty cables (Part 1), the completed cable must withstand a power-frequency AC test voltage of 3 kV for 5 minutes without insulation puncture.

Optional fire-resistant or FRLS sheathing must satisfy a minimum oxygen index of 29 percent, temperature index of 250°C under standard air, maximum acid gas generation of 20% by weight, and smoke density light transmission limits.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1554 (Part 1 & Part 2) : 1988 (Reaffirmed 2020) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing design, materials, dimensions, and testing requirements for PVC-insulated (heavy-duty) electric power and control cables. Part 1 covers low-voltage systems up to 1100 V, while Part 2 covers medium-voltage systems from 3.3 kV to 11 kV. Operating in close parallel with conductor code IS 8130 and PVC code IS 5831, the standard unifies the manufacturing of armoured and unarmoured cables. Incorporating active amendments (Amendment 5 for Part 1 and Amendment 4 for Part 2), the standard enforces a critical minimum 90 percent armour coverage calculated using trigonometric spiral formulas, and establishes a streamlined Type Approval Note 2 validation protocol—allowing successful test results of larger cable cross-sections to approve smaller sizes of the same design family, ensuring absolute energy efficiency and electrical safety across national grids.
